methodology_summary: Winners are selected on the published WrenchStack Fit Score: vertical fit (40%), aggregate user rating from G2 + Capterra (30%, excluded and reweighted when no listing exists), pricing transparency (15%) and integration coverage (15%), plus an editorial judgement on fit for the stated buyer profile. Corrected 2026-09-01: this summary previously described weights the code has never used (25% ratings and a 10% feature-depth factor). The live formula and its full changelog are on the methodology page, which is the authority. No vendor paid for placement. Where WrenchStack has an affiliate relationship with a winner, that is disclosed on the tool's review page, and recommendations are unchanged whether the affiliate is active or not.

categories.label: Best Overall FSM 2026
categories.why: Jobber wins overall on breadth and published pricing. It puts quoting, scheduling, invoicing, payments and customer communication in one app, with a mobile app for field work and a client portal where customers approve quotes and pay. It covers HVAC, plumbing, electrical, landscaping, cleaning, handyman and more, and plans start at $29/mo billed annually (Core, smallest team size) and rise with team size, with a 14-day free trial. The caveats: QuickBooks sync covers QuickBooks Online only and runs one way, and no plan advertises inventory management.
categories.buyer_signal: Best for small and mid-size home service businesses (1-30 people) that want quoting, scheduling, invoicing and payments in one app without enterprise complexity.

categories.label: Best Enterprise FSM 2026
categories.why: ServiceTitan wins enterprise on integrated depth for established trades shops: flat-rate pricebooks that can pull supplier price changes through Pricebook Connect, Marketing Pro attribution of calls, booked jobs and revenue down to the ad keyword, Dispatch Pro job assignment based on technician skills, location and conversion rates, membership management, payroll and commissions, in-app consumer financing and KPI reporting. The cost: ServiceTitan publishes no prices (third-party estimates put it at roughly $245 to $500 per technician per month), and third-party reports put full go-live at 3-6 months with a dedicated office admin running the project.
categories.buyer_signal: Best for established trades businesses (10+ people) with office staff and several technicians, where the cost of inefficiency now exceeds the cost of enterprise software.

categories.label: Best for HVAC 2026
categories.why: Sera Systems wins HVAC in the gap between entry-tier FSM such as Jobber and ServiceTitan's enterprise complexity and quote-only pricing. Built for residential HVAC, plumbing and electrical shops, it offers membership management, marketing attribution, a pricebook, consumer financing through Service Finance and KPI dashboards. Pricing is published: Core Essentials is $399/mo including unlimited admins and up to 4 technicians, then $149/mo per additional technician, plus an onboarding fee Sera does not publish.
categories.buyer_signal: Best for residential HVAC shops with teams of 5-25 that want trade-specific workflows and published pricing without enterprise complexity.

categories.label: Best for Plumbing 2026
categories.why: Workiz wins plumbing for service-call-heavy shops. Founded by former locksmiths, it is built around inbound, same-day work such as emergency plumbing: Genius Phone transcribes and summarizes calls and pulls job details from them, Genius Answering picks up missed calls and books jobs, and scheduling, dispatching and invoicing sit alongside lead integrations from Google Local Services Ads, Angi, Thumbtack and Yelp. Workiz now quotes all plans on request, AI features vary by plan or add-on, and the free trial is 7 days. Shops whose work is mostly scheduled maintenance should compare calendar-first tools.
categories.buyer_signal: Best for plumbing shops (1-15 people) whose work is mostly inbound, same-day calls, where answering and dispatching fast is the daily bottleneck.

categories.label: Best for Electrical 2026
categories.why: Housecall Pro wins electrical on its customer-facing tools and published pricing. Every plan includes scheduling and dispatch, quotes, invoicing, in-app card payments (from 2.59%), online booking, review requests and live phone and chat support, with consumer financing through Wisetack and Google Local Services Ads booking. Basic is $59/mo billed annually for 1 user, and Essentials at $149/mo covers 5 users and adds QuickBooks Online sync, flat-rate pricing and GPS tracking.
categories.buyer_signal: Best for residential electrical contractors (2-20 people) who want booking, payments, financing and review requests in one platform more than back-office accounting depth.

categories.label: Best for Roofing 2026
categories.why: AccuLynx wins roofing as CRM and project management software built for roofing contractors: insurance jobs with supplements and documents in the job file, measurement ordering from EagleView, Hover, Geospan or GAF QuickMeasure that populates the estimate, material ordering through QXO (Beacon), ABC Supply and SRS, production scheduling and crews, door-to-door sales workflows and AccuPay card and ACH payments. AccuLynx publishes no prices, so quotes come from sales, and Xactimate is not listed among its integrations.
categories.buyer_signal: Best for established roofing contractors (5-100 employees) doing insurance and storm restoration work who need claims-workflow depth.

categories.label: Best for SMB Roofing 2026
categories.why: Roofr wins SMB roofing on price and ease of getting started. There is a free Starter plan, and paid plans run from $109/mo (Measure+) to $349/mo (Scale) billed monthly, priced per company with unlimited users on every plan and, Roofr says, no setup fees. Its own roof measurement reports flow into proposals with on-the-spot e-signatures, a signed proposal becomes a material list, and invoices and card or ACH payments run in the same system. It is a lighter fit than AccuLynx for shops that want published prices; note that QuickBooks, crew management and job costing start on Scale, and Roofr runs as a web app rather than an App Store or Google Play download.
categories.buyer_signal: Best for solo roofers and small residential roofing teams (1-25 people) who want measurement, proposal and invoice in one system without enterprise overhead.

categories.label: Best for Landscaping 2026
categories.why: Aspire wins landscaping as software built for landscaping companies, covering grounds maintenance, landscape construction, and snow and ice management. Estimates are built from historical data and approved profit margins, and job costing with drill-down reporting shows how jobs perform against them; scheduling, a CRM, purchasing with inventory visibility, equipment maintenance tracking and an offline crew app for iOS and Android are built in. Pricing is custom-quoted: one monthly license fee with unlimited users that includes implementation, training and support, with electronic payments, payroll and GPS fleet management quoted on top.
categories.buyer_signal: Best for established landscape companies with multiple crews (20-500 people) running grounds maintenance, landscape construction or snow and ice work.

categories.label: Best for Cleaning 2026
categories.why: ZenMaid wins cleaning by being built for maid services and residential cleaning companies: recurring scheduling on a drag-and-drop calendar, automated confirmations and reminders by text and email, on-my-way notifications, invoicing and card payments through Stripe or Square, and a cleaner app with clock-in and clock-out. Pricing is per company rather than per cleaner: Starter is $19/mo for up to 40 appointments a month, and Pro ($39/mo) and Pro Max ($49/mo) have unlimited appointments. Text message charges are extra on every plan.
categories.buyer_signal: Best for residential cleaning and maid service businesses (1-30 people) that want scheduling, automated reminders and card payments at a low flat monthly price.

categories.label: Best for Pest Control 2026
categories.why: FieldRoutes wins pest control on recurring-route workflow. Built for pest control and lawn care companies, it covers recurring services, route optimization, drag-and-drop scheduling, automated reminders, billing with AutoPay, a customer payment portal, a technician mobile app, mobile sales and lead management, plus chemical and product tracking and Sentricon integration for termite work. Pricing is custom-quoted and based on your number of active customers rather than users, and there is no free trial, only a demo.
categories.buyer_signal: Best for pest control and lawn care companies (5-500 people) running recurring service routes that want scheduling, routing, sales and billing in one system.

categories.label: Best for Pool Service 2026
categories.why: Skimmer wins pool service by being built for pool and spa routes: techs log readings and dosages, checklists and photos in an offline-capable app, each body of water keeps a service history, and completed work flows into invoices with AutoPay and card or ACH payments. Pricing is per serviced location with unlimited users: Getting Started is $1 per location a month ($49 minimum), and Scaling Up at $2 per location ($98 minimum) adds route optimization, the Orenda LSI and dosing calculator and the LaMotte integration.
categories.buyer_signal: Best for pool and spa service businesses (1-50 people) that want chemical logging, service history, routing and recurring billing in one pool-specific app.

categories.label: Best for Solo Operators / 1-3 Users 2026
categories.why: Joist wins solo operators on price and simplicity. Billed monthly, Basics is $10/mo (up to 5 documents a month), Pro is $17/mo and Elite $32/mo, and annual billing gives two months free; the free plan has been discontinued. Even Basics includes online payments through Joist Payments and homeowner financing on estimates. Below the new Run plan ($100/mo list), which adds jobs and scheduling, Joist doesn't try to handle dispatching or team management, which suits the 1-3-person shop, and it is built mobile-first for quotes and invoices on site.
categories.buyer_signal: Best for solo contractors and 2-3-person operations doing residential service work without dispatch complexity.

categories.label: Best Value Entry-Tier 2026
categories.why: Service Fusion wins entry-tier value with flat per-company pricing and unlimited users on every plan: $208, $325 or $533/mo billed annually ($245, $382 or $627 month-to-month). That costs more than per-seat plans for a small team and can cost less for a large one, so price your own headcount. Starter already covers estimates, scheduling and dispatching, invoicing, integrated payments, QuickBooks integration, reporting and text messaging; inventory and job costing start on Plus, and no free trial is listed.
categories.buyer_signal: Best for cost-conscious shops with 5-50 people where per-user pricing math gets painful.

categories.label: Best Mobile UX 2026
categories.why: Housecall Pro wins mobile UX on the depth of its field app. Housecall Pro says its iOS and Android apps, available in English and Spanish, put job details, schedules and customer history on hand, handle clock-in and clock-out, quotes, and card, check, bank-transfer and financing payments, and keep working without Wi-Fi or signal. On the customer side it lists real-time notifications, invoices with payment links and a client portal.
categories.buyer_signal: Best for shops where field-tech adoption is the bottleneck and mobile-app polish matters more than back-office feature depth.

categories.label: Best Free Tier 2026
categories.why: Yardbook's Starter plan is free, with no subscription fee, and covers customers, jobs and scheduling, estimates, invoices, routing, expenses, reports and card payments. The catch is a 1% Yardbook fee on each online customer payment, on top of Stripe's card fees, which the $34.99/month Business plan waives; QuickBooks sync needs the $49.99/month Enterprise plan.
categories.buyer_signal: Best for solo landscapers and small lawn and landscape crews (1-5 people) who can't justify a monthly fee until revenue grows.

categories.label: Best CMMS 2026
categories.why: MaintainX wins CMMS on a mobile-first, offline-capable workflow with a free plan to start. Work orders, preventive maintenance, asset management, parts inventory, QR codes on assets and procedure templates run in apps built for techs in basements and on rooftops. The Basic plan is free with limits on recurring work and procedures, Essential is $20/user/mo billed annually ($25 monthly), Premium $65 ($75 monthly), and paid plans have a 30-day free trial. Integrations include SAP, Oracle, Microsoft Dynamics, QuickBooks, Slack and Power BI.
categories.buyer_signal: Best for internal facilities and maintenance teams (5-500 people) modernizing from paper/whiteboard or aging CMMS platforms, not contractors billing customers.

categories.label: Best Residential Construction PM 2026
categories.why: Buildertrend wins residential construction PM on homeowner-facing workflow for custom home builders and remodelers: selections for custom work, change orders with homeowner approval, a client portal where homeowners follow schedules, photos and selections, daily logs, subcontractor coordination, budgeting and job costing. One custom-quoted subscription includes unlimited users, every feature, onboarding and support, and it integrates with QuickBooks (Online and Desktop), Xero and Gusto.
categories.buyer_signal: Best for custom home builders, remodelers and specialty contractors (5-100 people) running multi-month projects with selections, change orders and a homeowner portal.

categories.label: Best Customer Support 2026
categories.why: Jobber wins customer support on openness: its help center is public, with step-by-step guides to scheduling, quoting, invoicing and payments, a Get Started section and guides to its App Marketplace integrations, and Jobber Academy offers free business articles, templates and calculators. Owners and crews can learn the product without going through sales.
categories.buyer_signal: Best for shops without IT staff who want to learn the software from public guides during ramp-up and ongoing operation.
